messages:
sara: Heads-up — private VPC customer (us-west-2) seeing big tail latency starting ~03:12 UTC. 95/99pct for text-gen jumped to ~350-700ms, throughput down ~35%. Not seeing obvious runtime OOMs.

mike: Thanks — which deployment? dedicated or private? any recent config/deploy?

sara: private (VPC, nat-egress via shared NAT GW). No code deploys in serving runtime at that time, only config rollouts earlier in the day (batching heuristic tweak).

anya: Pinging metrics now. Can you paste span_id or example request ids?

sara: span=f4a8c2 — attaching a snippet from the trace: latency spike aligns with >5s TCP retransmit bursts between worker and control-plane egress.

infra-bot: NAT-GW metrics: snat_port_utilization=92%, tcp_retransmits_up=3x baseline, flows_dropped=1.9%.

devon: SNAT port exhaustion + retransmits is classic noisy-neighbor NAT behavior. Could be large client-side payloads paired with DF flag/MTU mismatch causing excessive retransmits. Any big requests?

os: Runtime logs show sudden increase in avg request payload size (serialized tokens) — median request bytes up 4x during the window. Looks correlated with cache-miss ratio increase on KV cache.

luis: KV cache warmup note: we had canary for 'prefetch KV' toggle earlier. If we reverted to CPU-side KV reconstruction, that can increase request headers/context sizes when runtime reconstructs contexts. That plus larger batching could blow packet sizes.

mike: Can someone run tcpdump/traceroute on a worker in the affected VPC? Look for ICMP "fragmentation needed" and lots of retransmits.

anya: Ran quick tcpdump: lots of TCP retransmits and repeated MSS/DF set packets. Also intermittent ICMP Type3 Code4 (Fragmentation needed). Paste: ```15:04:24.123456 IP a.b.c.d. -> x.y.z. flags [DF], seq 12345, length 1460\n15:04:24.123789 IP x.y.z. > a.b.c.d. ICMP frag-needed, mtu 1400```

devon: That indicates PMTU issue. If packets marked DF are larger than path MTU, they get dropped if ICMP blocked. Are we blocking ICMP on firewall/NACL?

oz: Checking VPC NACL/SGs — no blanket ICMP deny rules in VPC, but customer-managed firewall appliance had deep-packet inspection that may drop ICMP. Also shared NAT GW does MSS clamping? default AWS NAT does not clamp MSS.

mike: Two likely contributors: 1) bigger payloads (KV cache miss + larger batches) causing DF packets > path MTU, 2) shared NAT SNAT port exhaustion causing retransmit/backoff latency. Need quick mitigations.

sara: Proposed mitigations — apply immediate runtime config rollback to cap batch size to 8, enable server-side MSS clamping on egress NAT (or set iptables --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on the NAT appliance), and spin up dedicated NAT (or add ENIs) for this customer if port exhaustion persists.

infra-bot: Created infra incident #INC-3421: added policy to enable MSS clamp on affected NAT appliances. Also provisioning additional NAT capacity (expected 12m).

luis: I can push a hotfix to runtime to treat KV cache-warmup requests as smaller batches (force small batch/serialize) so request byte size stays low until cache warms. Will ship a config flip.

anya: IETF suggestion: enable net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=2 as temporary measure on workers? That makes sender probe for smaller MTU to avoid DF drops. Might reduce throughput slightly but fixes fragmentation.

devon: Good call. Two-prong: infra applies MSS clamp + add NAT capacity, runtime reduces batch sizes for private VPCs + enable MTU probing.

oncall-bot: Action items assigned: infra->apply-mss-clamp (priority P0), infra->add-nat-capacity (P1), runtime->batch-cap-limit (P0), runtime->enable-mtu-probing (P1). Pager duty notified.

mike: After MSS clamp applied at 03:27 UTC and runtime batch cap at 03:30 UTC, we saw 95/99pct tail drop back toward baseline within ~8-15 minutes. SNAT util fell to 57% as additional capacity came up.

sara: Confirming: customer reported service restored. Will keep monitoring for 24h.

oz: Follow-up: need a permanent mitigation — customers on private/VPC should get either dedicated NAT capacity or guidance to allow ICMP/enable MSS-clamp on edge. Consider defaulting runtime batch heuristics in private deployments to smaller sizes to avoid large egress packets.

luis: Filed RFC-1487 (runtime batching defaults for private deployments) and INFRA-789 (NAT sizing + MSS-clamp policy).

anya: Will add dashboards: packet size distribution, KV cache hit-rate, and SNAT port utilization to the incident runbook.

sara: Closing notes: root cause = combination of KV cache warmups increasing request sizes + shared NAT SNAT port pressure + path MTU/ICMP blocking causing fragmentation and retransmits. Fix vector = MSS clamping + batch size cap + extra NAT capacity + runtime cache handling improvements.

mike: Nice work. Please add a short postmortem when the RFCs land. :thumbsup:
